text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland need not worry about the enlargement of NATO and it should trust its Western partners, Germany's Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said at a working meeting with Poland's Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati last weekend.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI

- Pope John Paul II met Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz in Krakow on Sunday to discuss Polish issues. The Pontiff and Cimoszewicz did not talk about the stalled concordat treaty between Poland and the Vatican.

- The presidents of central, east and south European countries including heads Austria, the Czech republic, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Poland, Slovakia and Slovenia met at a working meeting to discuss the enlargement of the EU and NATO in Piran, Slovenia last weekend.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- More than 190 computer firms will exhibit at the Warsaw computer fair to start tomorrow.

- The cabinet's economic ministers committee will discuss the restructuring programme of Poland's coke industry today. The industry's output will plunge by 50 percent in the next few years if the restructuring programme is not launched soon, a report by the Koksoprojekt coke industry research agency said.
- Poland will be the main investment target for France's Carrefour and Germany's Metro supermarket chains in 1997, the chains' presidents Daniel Bernard and Erwin Conradi said.
- Bad debts accrued by Polish consumer credit borrowers range between 3.0 percent and 6.0 percent of such credits at various banks, Polish banks say.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI

- The Pekpol SA meat processor and distributor will spend 25 million zlotys on distribution network development in 1997 and 1998, Pekpol's general shareholders meeting decided. The company is considering a convertible bond issue to partly finance the scheme.
- Around 200 Polish firms have opened branches in Belarus and 600 Polish-Belarussian joint ventures have been launched in there.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Spending on advertising on Polish television reached 1.2 billion zlotys in 1996. Around 52 percent of spending went to Channel One of the state-owned television (TVP1), 35 percent went to private Polsat Television, 11 percent was spent on spots screened by public television's Channel Two (TVP2) and 2.0 percent went to other stations.
ZYCIE

- U.S., German and international firms were the biggest direct investors in Poland last year. Foreign investments reached $300 per capita of Poland's population in the period, a report by the Foreign Investment Agency (PAIZ) said.
NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
